requiredText: Use the FGA CLI
Command Line Interface (CLI) enables you to interact with an FGA store, where you can manage tasks, create stores, and update FGA models, among other actions.
For instructions on installing it, visit the
Configuration
The CLI is configured to use a specific FGA server in one of three ways:
Using CLI flags.
Using environment variables.
configuration file, searched in the following order (highest to lowest priority):
Current working directory
User-specific config directory
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME
$HOME/.config
%AppData%
subdirectory under the user config directory
User's home directory
%USERPROFILE%
The API Url setting needs to point to the OpenFGA server:
FGA_API_URL
http://localhost:8080
provide the following parameters which appends the pre-shared key in the HTTP request header:
FGA_API_TOKEN
configure the following parameters based on the OIDC server that’s used to issue tokens:
FGA_CLIENT_ID
FGA_CLIENT_SECRET
FGA_API_SCOPES
FGA_API_TOKEN_ISSUER
FGA_API_AUDIENCE
A default store Id and authorization model Id can also be configured:
FGA_STORE_ID
FGA_MODEL_ID
All of the examples in this document assume the CLI is properly configured and that the Store ID is set either in an environment variable or the
Basic operations
The CLI commands below show you how to create a store and run your application’s most common operations, including how to write a model and write/delete/read tuples, and run queries.
Work with authorization model versions
each time a model is written to a store, a new version of the model is created.
All OpenFGA API endpoints receive an optional authorization model ID that points to a specific version of the model and defaults to the latest model version.
Always use a specific model ID and update it each time a new model version is used in production.
The following CLI commands lists the model Ids and find the latest one:
When using the CLI, the model ID can be specified as a
parameter or as part of the configuration.
Import tuples
It has the following parameters:
--max-tuples-per-write
(optional, default=1, max=40)
--max-parallel-requests
(optional, default=4)
--hide-imported-tuples
(optional, default=false)
Specifies the file name json, yaml and csv files are supported
The CLI returns a detailed JSON response that includes:
List of successfully written tuples
List of tuples that failed to write, including the error reason
Total number of tuples processed in this operation
Number of tuples successfully written
Number of tuples that failed to write
the successful tuples are not included in the output, making it more practical when importing large datasets.
Failed tuples are always shown to help identify and fix any issues.
greater than one, an error in one of the tuples implies none of the tuples get written.
Below are examples of the different file formats the CLI accepts when writing tuples:
yaml
JSON
CSV
When using the CSV format, you can omit certain headers, and you don’t need to specify the value for those fields.
Delete Tuples
To delete a tuple, specify the user/relation/object you want to delete.
To delete a group of tuples, specify a file that contains those tuples.

requiredText: Configure SDK Client Telemetry
The OpenFGA SDK Client supports telemetry data collection using
Enabling Telemetry
Install the OpenTelemetry SDK dependencies for your application
Instantiate the OpenTelemetry SDK in your application
Once you have completed these steps, the OpenFGA SDK Client will automatically collect telemetry data using your application's OpenTelemetry configuration.
Customizing Telemetry
The OpenFGA SDK Client will automatically use
for telemetry collection.
You can provide your own configuration to include additional metrics or to exclude metrics that are not relevant to your application.
Examples
We provide example applications for using telemetry with the OpenFGA SDK Client.
Supported Metrics
The OpenFGA SDK Client can collect the following metrics:
Metric Name
Enabled by Default
fga-client.request.duration
Histogram
Total request time for FGA requests, in milliseconds
fga-client.query.duration
Time taken by the FGA server to process and evaluate the request, in milliseconds
fga-client.credentials.request
Counter
Total number of new token requests initiated using the Client Credentials flow
Supported Attributes
The OpenFGA SDK Client can collect the following attributes:
Attribute Name
fga-client.request.client_id
Client ID associated with the request, if any
fga-client.request.method
FGA method/action that was performed (e.g., Check, ListObjects) in TitleCase
fga-client.request.model_id
Authorization model ID that was sent as part of the request, if any
fga-client.request.store_id
Store ID that was sent as part of the request
fga-client.response.model_id
Authorization model ID that the FGA server used
fga-client.user
User associated with the action of the request for check and list users
http.client.request.duration
Duration for the SDK to complete the request, in milliseconds
http.host
Host identifier of the origin the request was sent to
http.request.method
HTTP method for the request
http.request.resend_count
Number of retries attempted, if any
http.response.status_code
Status code of the response
http.server.request.duration
url.scheme
HTTP scheme of the request
url.full
Full URL of the request
user_agent.original
User Agent used in the query
Tracing
tracing with OpenTelemetry.
If your application uses OpenTelemetry tracing, traces will be propagated to OpenFGA, provided the traces are exported to the same address.
This can be useful to help diagnose any suspected performance issues when using OpenFGA.
If your application does not already use tracing, OpenTelemetry offers
for several languages.

requiredText: Immutable Authorization Models
Authorization Models in OpenFGA are immutable, they are created once and then can no longer be deleted or modified.
Each time you write an authorization model, a new version is created.
Viewing all the authorization models
You can list all the authorization models for a store using the
This endpoint returns the results sorted in reverse chronological order, as in the first model in the list is the latest model.
By default, only the last 50 models are returned, but you can paginate across by passing in the appropriate
continuation_token
How to target a particular model
Some endpoints relating to tuples
authorization_model_id
which we strongly recommend passing, especially in production.
In practice, you would pin the authorization model ID alongside the store ID in your configuration management system.
Your services would read this value and use it in their requests to FGA.
This helps you ensure that your services are using the same consistent ID across all your applications, and that rollouts can be seamless.
Benefits of passing in an authorization model ID
Targeting a specific model ID would ensure that you don't accidentally break your authorization checks in production because a mistake was made when updating the authorization model.
It would also slightly improve the latency on your check requests.
If that field is passed, evaluation and validation will happen for that particular authorization model ID.
If this field is not passed, OpenFGA will use the last created Authorization Model for that store.
Potential use-cases
Complex model migrations
Certain model changes require adapting your application code and migrating tuples before rolling it out.
For example, if you rename a relation, you need to change the application and copy the existing tuples to use the new relation name.
This scenario requires the following steps:
Update the authorization model with the renamed relation. A new model ID will be generated but it won't be used in production yet.
Update the application to use the new relation name.
Copy existing tuples to use the new relation name.
Deploy the new application targeting the new model ID.
You can learn more about model migrations
Progresivelly rollout changes
Being able to target multiple versions of the authorization model enables you to progressively roll out model changes, which is something you should consider doing if the changes are significant.

Do shadow checks where you would perform checks against both your existing model and the new upcoming model you are hoping to replace it with.This will help you detect and resolve any accidental discrepancies you may be introducing, and ensure that your new model is at least as good as your old one.

When you are confident with your model, you could implement gradual rollouts that would allow you to monitor and check if any users are having access issues before you go ahead and increase the rollout to 100% of your user base.
